name: Canadian Energy Transition Risk Index (CETR Index)
description: A quantitative, open-source composite indicator scoring Canada's ten provinces on their exposure to risks arising from the global energy transition. Higher scores indicate greater risk.
normalization_rationale: Percentile rank selected over z-score because N=10 provinces is too small for the normality assumption. Robust to Alberta's extreme outlier values on the stranded asset component. Recommended by OECD Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators (2008) for small-N comparisons.

carbon_intensity.label: Carbon Intensity
carbon_intensity.description: Electricity sector CO2 emissions per megawatt-hour generated. Captures how carbon-locked the province's current power grid is — higher intensity means greater exposure to carbon pricing and regulatory risk as the grid must decarbonize.
carbon_intensity.source_primary: ECCC National GHG Inventory, Annex 13 Table A13-5 (Electricity and Heat Production by Province)
carbon_intensity.source_secondary: Canada Energy Regulator — Electricity Generation Dataset

stranded_asset_risk.label: Stranded Asset Risk
stranded_asset_risk.description: Fossil fuel industries (oil & gas extraction, coal mining, petroleum manufacturing, support services) as a percentage of total provincial GDP. Captures economic exposure if fossil fuel assets are devalued by policy, technology shift, or reduced demand under the energy transition.
stranded_asset_risk.source_primary: Statistics Canada Table 36-10-0402-01 — GDP by industry by province (annual)
naics_labels: Services to oil and gas extraction

grid_reliability.label: Grid Reliability
grid_reliability.description: SAIDI (System Average Interruption Duration Index) — average hours of power outage per customer per year. Higher unreliability increases the economic cost of electrification and reduces the viability of transitioning to electric heating and transport.
grid_reliability.source_primary: Canadian Electricity Association — Electricity Reliability Report (Annual)
grid_reliability.note: Only source requiring manual PDF extraction. Flag in pipeline if format changes.

energy_poverty.label: Energy Poverty
energy_poverty.description: Percentage of provincial households spending more than 6% of gross household income on energy (electricity + heating fuel). Higher energy poverty rates indicate vulnerable households that would be most exposed to transition costs (carbon pricing, utility rate increases from grid investment).
energy_poverty.threshold_rationale: 6% threshold is the standard low-income energy burden threshold used by NRCan, Efficiency Canada, and academic literature. Above 6% is considered energy poverty.
energy_poverty.source_primary: Statistics Canada Survey of Household Spending, Table 11-10-0223-01

workforce_exposure.label: Workforce Exposure
workforce_exposure.description: Fossil fuel industry employment as a percentage of total provincial workforce. Captures human capital risk — provinces with high fossil fuel employment face greater social disruption, retraining costs, and political resistance to transition.
workforce_exposure.source_primary: Statistics Canada Labour Force Survey, Table 14-10-0023-01

excluded_territories_rationale: Insufficient electricity grid data and fundamentally different energy systems (diesel microgrids). Planned for v2.

sensitivity_analysis.description: Index scores computed under all four normalization methods. Methodology considered robust if Spearman rank correlation between any two methods exceeds 0.90.

monetary_valuation.description: Supplementary monetary valuation of stranded asset risk expressed as % of provincial GDP. Not used in primary index score.
monetary_valuation.method: Carbon budget approach following Carbon Tracker methodology
monetary_valuation.reference: Carbon Tracker Initiative (2021); Caldecott et al. (2016)

references.oecd_handbook: OECD/JRC (2008). Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators: Methodology and User Guide. OECD Publishing.
references.wef_eti: Singh et al. (2019). The energy transitions index: An analytic framework. Energy Strategy Reviews, 26.
references.tcfd: TCFD (2018). Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures.
references.pembina: Pembina Institute. Climate change and the financial risk of stranded assets.
